diagnostic_evidence.quote: it admits a Cholesky decomposition $I_n-A^\top A = LL^\top $ with $L\in \f R^{n\times s}$
$\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A=U^\top V$ be the decomposition given in Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal_decomposition}
Theorem \ref{th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones} says that $\PSV(A,P,Q)$ can be reduced in polynomial time to $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes the equivalence of optimal values/solutions once U and V are given. The generators of the MA instance are the columns of V=[A/||A||; L^T], which involve the spectral norm ||A|| and a Cholesky factor of I - A^T A/||A||^2; these are in general irrational even for integer A (e.g. the {1,-d} biclique matrices used in Corollary cor:angles_cones_NPhard). Hence the MA instance cannot be written down with polynomial-size rational data, and 'polynomial-time reduction' in the standard (bit) model is not established; the NP-hardness of MA(P,Q) for polyhedral cones with rational generators is therefore not proved as written.

failure_location.quote: Then, $\SV(A,P,Q)$ reduces in polynomial time to $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$ where $\wt P:=UP$ and $\wt Q:=VQ$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either state explicitly that the reduction is in a real-number model, or give a rational reduction: scale A by a rational alpha with ||alpha A||<1, factor I - alpha^2 A^T A = L D L^T with rational L, D and expand each sqrt(d_j) via a rational four-squares representation into four rows, yielding rational U,V with U^T V = alpha A and V^T V = I in dimension at most m+4n; then rerun the equivalence argument.
issues.overall_effect: The headline NP-hardness claim for the maximal-angle problem MA(P,Q) (abstract, Section 2) rests on an unestablished polynomial-time reduction; only a real-RAM-style equivalence is proved.
issues.title: Reduction SV -> MA claimed polynomial-time but produces irrational (non-encodable) cone data
issues.why_classification: A contained new construction restores the NP-hardness claim in the standard model without changing the results' scope, but it is a genuine nontrivial addition rather than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \langle u, A v^*\rangle \ge \langle u^*, A v^*\rangle, \qquad \langle u^*, A v\rangle \ge \langle u^*, A v^*\rangle, \qquad \forall\, (u, v)\in P\times Q : \|u\| = \|v\| = 1.
Observe that the above means that $u^*$ solves $\SV(A,P,\mathbb R_+ v^*)$ and $v^*$ solves $\SV(A,\R_+ u^*,Q)$.

issues.failure_explanation: A Nash pair requires u* to be a global minimizer of <u,Av*> over unit u in P. A local minimizer of the joint problem only gives a local minimizer in u. These differ when the value is positive: take A=I, P=R^3_+, Q=R_+(1,1,1.5). With v fixed, u=e_3 is a local minimizer of <u,v> over unit u in R^3_+ (all feasible directions increase the objective), so (e_3,v) is a local minimum of the joint problem, but <e_1,v> < <e_3,v>, so it is not a Nash pair. The observation is thus false in general (it holds for local minima with negative value).

failure_location.quote: Observe also that any solution pair and all local minima of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ are Nash pairs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the observation to solution pairs (and to local minima whose value is negative), or delete the local-minima clause.
issues.overall_effect: Only the side remark is wrong; Proposition pro:nonnegative_case_SVcones uses only that solution pairs are Nash pairs, which is correct.
issues.title: False claim that all local minima of SV(A,P,Q) are Nash pairs
issues.why_classification: Local rewording; no result depends on the false clause.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Observe that $-\Vert A\Vert\leq \langle u,Av\rangle\leq\Vert A\Vert$ for all feasible pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$.
the optimal value of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is the minimum entry of $G^\top A H$

issues.failure_explanation: The stated equivalence fails in one direction: if P=R_+g and Q=R_+h with g^T A h >= 0 but g^T A h < ||A|| (e.g. A=I in R^2, g=e_1, h=(1,1)/sqrt2 giving 1/sqrt2 < 1), both cones have one generator and G^T A H is a 1x1 nonnegative matrix, yet the optimal value is not ||A||. The correct condition is that both cones are rays and g^T A h = ||A||.

failure_location.quote: the case $\langle u, Av\rangle =    \|A\|$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by: P and Q are single rays g,h with g^T A h = ||A||.
issues.overall_effect: Only the informal check for the extreme case lambda*=||A|| is misstated; this case is anyway covered by the preprocessing Case 1 (lambda* >= 0).
issues.title: Incorrect characterization of the case lambda* = ||A||
issues.why_classification: One-line correction of a side remark with no dependents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $(u,v)$ be a local minimum of $\MA(P, Q)$ with $u \neq -v$ in dimension $n\le 3$. Then $u$ or $v$ is a generator of its respective cone.
Notice that this case coincides with the condition $P\cap (-Q)\ne \{0\}$ when $A=I$.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary assumes u != -v; the prose drops this hypothesis. When P and -Q intersect nontrivially the optimal value is -1 with u=-v, and neither u nor v need be a generator: in R^3 take P=R^3_+ and Q=-cone{(1,1,-eps),(-eps,1,1),(1,-eps,1)} with small eps>0. Then (1,1,1) is in P and -Q, so the maximal angle is pi, but no e_i lies in -Q and no generator of Q lies in -P, so min_i MA(R_+g_i,Q) and min_j MA(P,R_+h_j) are strictly greater than -1. The claimed reduction therefore fails in this case.

failure_location.quote: Corollary~\ref{cor:local_minimum_angles_have_generators_in_dim3} tells us that any solution $(u^*,v^*)$ of $\MA(P, Q)$ in dimension $3$ or less contains at least a generator. As a consequence, the minimum over the optimal values of $\MA(\f R_+g_i,Q)$ and $\MA(P,\f R_+ h_j)$ over all $i,j$ correspond to the maximum angle of $\MA(P, Q)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis u* != -v* (equivalently P∩(-Q)={0}) to the prose, and note that the antipodal case is detected by the Case-2 preprocessing test.
issues.overall_effect: The stated polynomial-time procedure for MA(P,Q) in dimension <= 3 is incomplete unless the case P∩(-Q) != {0} is checked separately (which the preprocessing of Section subs:preprocessing can do).
issues.title: Dimension <= 3 reduction to generator subproblems omits the antipodal case u = -v
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard, already-available preprocessing condition restores the claim without changing any method or result.
